slides.title: What Is Object-Oriented Programming
slides.content: OOP organizes software around objects that combine data and behavior. The four main pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.
slides.example: class Car { int Speed; void Accelerate() { } }
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Objects and Classes
slides.content: A class is a blueprint. An object is an instance created from that blueprint with its own data.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Encapsulation Basics
slides.content: Encapsulation hides internal state and exposes only necessary operations through public methods or properties.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: State and Behavior
slides.content: Objects store state in fields and expose behavior through methods. This keeps related data and logic together.
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: Add a field 'radius' and a method 'Diameter' that returns 2 * radius.
hints: The field needs a type. Use double, the same type as radius in the example.
Diameter should equal 2 * radius. Fill the second blank with 2.

slides.title: Abstraction in OOP
slides.content: Abstraction exposes only essential features and hides complexity. Abstract classes and interfaces are common tools.
slides.example:
abstract class Shape { public abstract double Area(); }
class Square : Shape { public override double Area() => Side * Side; }
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

slides.title: Inheritance Basics
slides.content: Inheritance allows a derived class to reuse and extend a base class. It supports an is-a relationship.
slides.example:
class Animal { public void Eat() { } }
class Cat : Animal { public void Meow() { } }
slides.exampleOutput: Class definition; produces no console output.

exercise.prompt: A Cat _____ Animal, so Cat inherits Eat().

slides.title: Polymorphism Overview
slides.content: Polymorphism lets you treat different objects through a common interface. Overriding base methods enables runtime behavior selection.

exercise.prompt: Drag the keyword used to override a base method: public override double Area() [?]

slides.title: OOP Review
slides.content: OOP models real-world ideas as objects with state and behavior. Use encapsulation to protect data and inheritance to share logic.
